choices.text: The student is right - the membrane blocks everything
The membrane is selectively permeable: food and oxygen cross in, waste crosses out, and some things are kept out
Cells have no membrane, so everything drifts in and out
Only water can cross a membrane; nothing else moves

questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving. Reteach point: The membrane is selectively permeable: it lets some things through and keeps others out. A walled-off cell would starve: nothing in, nothing out.
questions.misconception: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving.
questions.prompt: A student says nothing can enter or leave a cell because its membrane is a solid wall. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: It means the membrane chooses what crosses it: some substances are let through while others are kept out.
questions.feedback: A strong answer uses the choosing idea: let some through, keep others out. An answer saying the membrane blocks everything, or lets everything through, has missed the choosing.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what selectively permeable means for a cell membrane.

choices.text: Its wall grows thicker when it rains
Its full vacuole pushes the membrane hard against the cell wall
Its nucleus pumps the cell up

questions.feedback: The push comes from the water-filled vacuole pressing the membrane against the wall. Lose the water and the cell goes flaccid.
questions.prompt: A plant cell is turgid and firm because...

questions.feedback: The ladder climbs cell to tissue to organ to system: each level is built from the one below it.
questions.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest: organ, cell, system, tissue.
